concepts.title: Heegaard splittings and diagrams
concepts.blurb: Every closed orientable 3-manifold $Y$ admits a Heegaard splitting $Y = U_g\cup_{\Sigma_g} U_g'$ as the union of two genus-$g$ handlebodies glued along a common surface $\Sigma_g$. Encoding the gluing by attaching curves on $\Sigma_g$ — an $\alpha$-system bounding disks in $U_g$ and a $\beta$-system in $U_g'$ — produces a Heegaard diagram $(\Sigma_g,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta)$. Reidemeister–Singer: any two diagrams of $Y$ are related by stabilisation and handleslides.

concepts.title: Lagrangian Floer homology
concepts.blurb: Given two transversely intersecting Lagrangians $L_0,L_1$ in a symplectic manifold $(X,\omega)$, the Floer chain complex $CF(L_0,L_1)$ is generated by $L_0\cap L_1$ with differential counting index-1 pseudoholomorphic Whitney disks running boundary arcs on $L_0,L_1$. Floer's miracle: $\partial^2=0$ and the homology $HF(L_0,L_1)$ is invariant under Hamiltonian isotopy. Its dimension bounds the Arnold-conjecture intersection counts.

concepts.title: Heegaard Floer variants
concepts.blurb: Apply Lagrangian Floer to the two tori $\mathbb{T}_\alpha,\mathbb{T}_\beta\subset\mathrm{Sym}^g(\Sigma_g)$ inside the symmetric product of the Heegaard surface. A basepoint $z$ records $U$-multiplicities; four variants $\widehat{HF},\,HF^-,\,HF^+,\,HF^\infty$ arise from different localisations in $U$. They decompose along $\mathrm{Spin}^c$-structures and fit in long exact sequences relating $\widehat{HF}$ to $HF^\pm$ and $HF^\pm$ to $HF^\infty$.

concepts.title: Knot Floer homology
concepts.blurb: A doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(S^3,K)$ filters the chain complex by the Alexander grading. The homology $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ is bigraded by Maslov $M$ and Alexander $A$ gradings and categorifies the Alexander polynomial: $\Delta_K(t)=\sum_{M,A}(-1)^M\dim\widehat{HFK}_M(K,A)\,t^A$. It detects the Seifert genus, fiberedness, and the unknot — none of which $\Delta_K$ alone sees.

concepts.title: The $d$-invariant (correction term)
concepts.blurb: For a rational homology sphere $Y$ and $\mathfrak{s}\in\mathrm{Spin}^c(Y)$, $HF^+(Y,\mathfrak{s})$ contains a tower $\mathcal{T}^+$ whose lowest grading is the $d$-invariant $d(Y,\mathfrak{s})\in\mathbb{Q}$. It obstructs $Y$ from bounding a $\mathbb{Q}$-homology ball and satisfies a cobordism inequality involving any negative-definite filling. For lens spaces $L(p,1)$ the closed formula is $d=\tfrac{(2i-p)^2}{4p}-\tfrac14$.

concepts.title: Surgery exact triangle and cobordism maps
concepts.blurb: A 4-dimensional cobordism $W:Y_0\rightsquigarrow Y_1$ induces a map $F_W:HF^\circ(Y_0)\to HF^\circ(Y_1)$, functorial under composition. For a knot $K\subset Y$ and framing $n$, the three manifolds $Y,Y_n(K),Y_{n+1}(K)$ — Dehn fillings along slopes pairwise distance 1 — fit in a surgery exact triangle $\widehat{HF}(Y)\to\widehat{HF}(Y_n)\to\widehat{HF}(Y_{n+1})\to\widehat{HF}(Y)[-1]$ proved by counting holomorphic triangles.

concepts.title: The $\tau$-invariant and slice-genus bounds
concepts.blurb: The $\tau$-invariant $\tau(K)\in\mathbb{Z}$ extracted from the Alexander-graded $\widehat{HFK}$ gives a smooth slice-genus bound $|\tau(K)|\le g_4(K)$ and a homomorphism from the concordance group $\mathcal{C}\to\mathbb{Z}$. For torus knots $\tau(T(p,q))=(p-1)(q-1)/2=g_4(T(p,q))$, recovering Kronheimer–Mrowka's Milnor-conjecture result. Combined with Donaldson, $d$ and $\tau$ obstruct smooth structures and detect exotic 4-manifolds.
